subject: science
question: The substance from which an object is made is called its:
hint: A chair may be made of wood, plastic or steel. Wood, plastic and steel are the materials.

subject: science
question: Materials through which you can see clearly are called:
hint: Transparent materials such as clear glass let light pass straight through.

subject: science
question: Materials through which you cannot see at all are called:
hint: Opaque materials such as wood, stone and metal block light completely.

subject: science
question: Materials through which you can see only partly are called:
hint: Translucent materials such as butter paper and frosted glass let some light through but blur the view.

subject: science
question: Which of these is a transparent material?
hint: You can read printed words through clear glass, so it is transparent.

subject: science
question: Which of these is translucent?
hint: Butter paper lets light through but you cannot see a sharp image through it.

subject: science
question: Why are window panes usually made of transparent glass?
options: To let light into the room while keeping wind and dust out
hint: The property chosen for a job depends on the need. Here, light must pass but air must not.

subject: science
question: The shine seen on the surface of some materials is called:
hint: Lustre is the shine typical of metals such as gold, silver and freshly cut iron.

subject: science
question: Materials that have a shine are said to be:
hint: Lustrous materials shine. Wood, chalk and cloth are non-lustrous.

subject: science
question: Which of these materials is lustrous?
hint: Metals are usually lustrous. Chalk, wood and paper have dull surfaces.

subject: science
question: Old iron articles lose their shine because:
options: A layer of rust forms on the surface
hint: Moist air causes rusting, and the rough rust layer hides the shiny metal beneath.

subject: science
question: How a material feels when you touch it is called its:
hint: Texture describes whether a surface feels rough, smooth, soft or grainy.

subject: science
question: Which of these has a rough texture?
hint: Sandpaper feels gritty because tiny hard grains are stuck to its surface.

subject: science
question: The three common states in which matter exists are:
hint: Matter is normally found as a solid, a liquid or a gas.

subject: science
question: Which state of matter has a fixed shape and a fixed volume?
hint: Solids keep both their shape and their volume because their particles are packed tightly.

subject: science
question: Which state of matter has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container?
hint: Water poured into any vessel takes that shape, yet one litre stays one litre.

subject: science
question: Which state of matter has neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume?
hint: A gas spreads out to fill whatever container it is put in.

subject: science
question: In which state are the particles of matter packed most closely together?
options: They are the same in all states
hint: Particles are tightly packed in solids, loosely arranged in liquids and far apart in gases.

subject: science
question: Which of these can be compressed most easily?
hint: Gas particles have large gaps between them, so a gas can be squeezed into a smaller space.

subject: science
question: Ice, water and steam are:
options: Three states of the same substance
hint: They are all water. Only the state changes as heat is added or removed.

subject: science
question: Sorting materials into groups is useful because it:
options: Helps us find things easily and study their properties
hint: Grouping similar things together makes them easier to locate, compare and study.

subject: science
question: A shopkeeper keeps all the soaps on one shelf and all the biscuits on another. This is an example of:
hint: Grouping similar items together is exactly what scientists do when they classify materials.

subject: science
question: Which property of glass makes it unsuitable for making a cricket bat?
options: It is brittle and breaks easily
hint: A bat must take heavy blows. A brittle material would shatter.

subject: science
question: Why are cooking vessels usually not made of transparent plastic?
options: Plastic melts and deforms at cooking temperatures
hint: A material must suit the job. Cooking needs a material that stands high heat.

subject: science
question: Which of these objects is made of more than one material?
hint: A pencil has a wooden body, a graphite lead, sometimes a metal ring and a rubber eraser.

subject: science
question: The same object can often be made from different materials. A bucket can be made of:
hint: Many materials can do the same job. The choice depends on cost, weight and durability.

subject: science
question: Which of these is a gas at room temperature?
hint: Oxygen is a gas. Mercury is a liquid metal, and ice and copper are solids.

subject: science
question: Which metal is a liquid at room temperature?
hint: Mercury is the only common metal that is liquid at room temperature.

subject: science
question: Smoke coming out of a chimney is an example of a:
hint: Smoke is hot gas with very fine solid particles of unburnt carbon floating in it.

subject: science
question: Which property would you test to decide whether a material is suitable for making a mirror?
options: Whether its surface is smooth and lustrous
hint: A mirror needs a smooth shiny surface so that light bounces off evenly.

subject: science
question: Materials that cannot be easily compressed, cut or scratched are said to be:
hint: Hardness is a measure of how well a material resists being scratched or dented.

subject: science
question: Which of these is the hardest natural substance known?
hint: Diamond scratches every other natural material and is used in cutting tools.

subject: science
question: Which of these is a soft material?
hint: A sponge can be squeezed and pressed easily, so it is soft.

subject: science
question: A simple way to compare the hardness of two materials is to:
options: See which one scratches the other
hint: The harder material scratches the softer one. This is the basis of the hardness scale.

subject: science
question: Why are cutting tools often tipped with diamond?
options: Diamond is extremely hard and can cut other materials
hint: Only a harder material can cut a hard one, and diamond is the hardest available.

subject: science
question: The mass of a material present in a given volume is called its:
hint: Density compares how much matter is packed into a certain space.

subject: science
question: An object floats in water if its density is:
options: More than the density of water
Less than the density of water
hint: Objects less dense than water float. Denser ones sink.

subject: science
question: Which of these floats on water?
hint: Wood is less dense than water, so it floats.

subject: science
question: Which of these sinks in water?
hint: Iron is much denser than water, so an iron nail sinks.

subject: science
question: A huge iron ship floats on water, but a small iron nail sinks. Why?
options: Sea water is not real water
The ship is hollow, so its overall density is less than water
hint: Density depends on the whole object, not the material alone. The air inside the hull lowers the ship's overall density.

subject: science
question: Oil poured into water forms a layer on top because oil is:
hint: The less dense liquid always settles above the denser one.

subject: science
question: Which of these has the highest density?
hint: Iron packs far more mass into the same volume than wood, cork or thermocol.

subject: science
question: Two blocks have the same size, but one is heavier. The heavier block has:
hint: For the same volume, more mass means more density.

subject: science
question: Why does a dry leaf float on water while a green stone sinks?
options: The leaf is less dense than water and the stone is more dense
hint: Floating and sinking depend on density compared with water, not on size or colour.

subject: science
question: Life jackets are filled with light material so that the wearer:
options: Has a lower overall density and floats
hint: Trapped light material lowers the total density of the person and jacket together.

subject: science
question: Which of these would you use to measure the volume of an irregular stone?
options: A measuring cylinder with water, noting the rise in level
hint: The stone pushes aside its own volume of water, so the rise in level gives the volume.

subject: science
question: Rubber is chosen for making tyres mainly because it is:
options: Tough yet flexible and grips the road
hint: Tyres must bend without breaking and grip the road, so a tough flexible material is needed.

subject: science
question: Cotton is preferred for summer clothes because it is:
hint: Cotton is soft against skin and soaks up sweat, which then evaporates and cools you.

subject: science
question: A material that can be beaten into thin sheets is said to be:
hint: Malleable metals such as gold and aluminium can be hammered flat without cracking.

subject: science
question: A material that can be drawn into thin wires is said to be:
hint: Ductile metals such as copper can be stretched into long wires.

subject: science
question: A material that breaks suddenly into pieces when hammered is said to be:
hint: Brittle materials such as glass and chalk shatter instead of bending.

subject: science
question: Which property of gold allows it to be beaten into very thin foil for decoration?
hint: Gold is the most malleable metal and can be hammered into sheets thinner than paper.

subject: science
question: Why is glass unsuitable for making a hammer?
options: It is brittle and would shatter on impact
hint: A hammer must absorb repeated blows. Brittle materials crack instead.

subject: science
question: Thermocol is used for packing delicate items because it is:
hint: A soft, light, cushioning material protects fragile goods during transport.

subject: science
question: Two identical bottles are filled, one with oil and one with water. Which weighs more?
options: It cannot be decided at all
The bottle of water, because water is denser than oil
hint: For the same volume, the denser liquid has more mass. Water is denser than cooking oil.

subject: science
question: A ball of clay sinks in water, but the same clay shaped into a bowl floats. This shows that floating depends on:
options: How long the clay is kept in water
The overall density of the object, including trapped air
hint: Shaping the clay into a bowl traps air, lowering the object's overall density below that of water.

subject: science
question: Aluminium is preferred over iron for making aircraft bodies mainly because it is:
hint: Aircraft need strength with low weight, so a strong metal of low density is chosen.

subject: science
question: Which of these is not a property used to describe a material?
hint: Price is decided by people and markets. Hardness, solubility and density are physical properties of the material itself.

subject: science
question: A stone and a sponge of the same size are dropped in water. What happens?
options: The stone sinks and the sponge floats at first
hint: The sponge has air trapped in its pores, giving it a low overall density until it soaks up water.

subject: science
question: A substance that dissolves completely in water is said to be:
hint: Soluble substances such as sugar and salt disappear into water to form a clear solution.

subject: science
question: Which of these is soluble in water?
hint: Sugar disappears into water and cannot be seen. Sand and chalk stay as visible particles.

subject: science
question: Which of these is insoluble in water?
hint: Sand settles at the bottom no matter how long you stir, so it is insoluble.

subject: science
question: The substance that dissolves in a solution is called the:
hint: In sugar solution, sugar is the solute and water is the solvent.

subject: science
question: The liquid in which a substance dissolves is called the:
hint: The solvent does the dissolving. In most everyday solutions it is water.

subject: science
question: In salt solution, common salt is the:
hint: Salt is the substance being dissolved, so it is the solute.

subject: science
question: Sugar dissolves faster in hot water than in cold water because:
options: Heating helps the particles mix more quickly
Sugar melts in hot water only
hint: Warmer water particles move faster, so the solute spreads through it sooner.

subject: science
question: Which of these would help sugar dissolve faster in water?
hint: Stirring, heating and using finer particles all speed up dissolving.

subject: science
question: Powdered sugar dissolves faster than sugar cubes because:
options: Powder has more surface in contact with water
hint: Breaking a solid into smaller pieces exposes more surface to the solvent.

subject: science
question: Two liquids that mix completely with each other are said to be:
hint: Miscible liquids such as milk and water blend into one uniform liquid.

subject: science
question: Two liquids that do not mix and form separate layers are:
hint: Oil and water are immiscible. They separate into layers after standing.

subject: science
question: Which pair of liquids is immiscible?
hint: Oil floats as a separate layer on water and will not blend with it.

subject: science
question: Which of these gases dissolves in water and is essential for fish?
hint: Fish use their gills to take in the oxygen dissolved in water.

subject: science
question: Bubbles rising in a fizzy drink when the bottle is opened show that:
options: A gas was dissolved in the liquid
hint: Carbon dioxide is dissolved under pressure. Opening the bottle releases the pressure and the gas escapes.

subject: science
question: A solution in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature is called:
hint: Once a solution is saturated, extra solute simply settles at the bottom.

subject: science
question: How can you dissolve more sugar in an already saturated sugar solution?
hint: Solubility usually rises with temperature, so heating lets the solution hold more solute.

subject: science
question: Water is called the universal solvent because it:
options: Dissolves a very large number of substances
hint: Water dissolves more substances than any other common liquid, though not literally everything.

subject: science
question: When chalk powder is stirred into water and left to stand, it:
hint: Chalk is insoluble. Its particles stay suspended for a while and then settle.

subject: science
question: A clear sugar solution is transparent because:
options: The sugar particles are far too small to be seen
hint: In a true solution the solute breaks into particles so tiny that light passes straight through.

subject: science
question: If you dissolve 10 g of salt in water and then evaporate all the water, how much salt do you get back?
hint: Dissolving does not destroy the solute. Evaporating the solvent leaves it behind.

subject: science
question: Which of these is a solution?
hint: A true solution is uniform and clear, with no visible separate particles.

subject: science
question: Kerosene is used to remove grease stains because grease is:
options: Soluble in kerosene but not in water
hint: Different solvents dissolve different substances. Water fails on grease, but kerosene works.

subject: science
question: Which of these is a solution of a gas in a liquid?
hint: Soda water is carbon dioxide gas dissolved in water.

subject: science
question: Why can fish not survive in boiled and cooled water kept in a sealed jar?
options: Boiling drives out the dissolved oxygen
hint: Heating reduces the solubility of gases, so boiling removes the dissolved oxygen fish need.

subject: science
question: Which of these does not dissolve in water?
hint: Oil is immiscible with water and forms a separate layer instead of dissolving.

subject: science
question: A dilute solution is one that contains:
options: A small amount of solute in a large amount of solvent
hint: Dilute means weak. Concentrated means a lot of solute in the same amount of solvent.

subject: science
question: Sea water tastes salty because it contains:
hint: Rivers carry dissolved minerals to the sea, where they build up over long periods.

subject: science
question: You stir salt into water until no more dissolves. Some salt remains at the bottom. The solution is:
hint: Undissolved solute lying at the bottom is the sign of a saturated solution.

subject: science
question: Which everyday activity depends on a substance being soluble in water?
options: Using a magnet to pick up pins
hint: Making a drink relies on the sugar dissolving evenly through the water.

subject: science
question: Materials that allow electricity to pass through them are called:
hint: Metals such as copper and aluminium are good conductors of electricity.

subject: science
question: Materials that do not allow electricity to pass through them are called:
hint: Rubber, plastic and wood are insulators and are used to cover live wires.

subject: science
question: Which of these is a good conductor of electricity?
hint: Copper conducts electricity well, which is why it is used inside electrical wires.

subject: science
question: Electrical wires are covered with plastic because plastic:
options: Is an insulator and prevents electric shocks
hint: The metal inside carries the current and the plastic outside keeps it from reaching your hand.

subject: science
question: Materials that allow heat to pass through them easily are called:
hint: Metals conduct heat well, which is why cooking vessels are made of them.

subject: science
question: Cooking vessels are usually made of metal because metals:
options: Conduct heat quickly to the food
hint: Heat must pass from the flame through the vessel into the food, so a good heat conductor is needed.

subject: science
question: The handles of cooking pans are often made of wood or plastic because these materials:
hint: A poor conductor stops heat from reaching your hand, so the handle stays cool.

subject: science
question: Which of these is a poor conductor of heat?
hint: Wood does not carry heat well, which is why wooden spoons are safe for stirring hot food.

subject: science
question: Materials that are attracted by a magnet are called:
hint: Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials.

subject: science
question: Which of these is attracted by a magnet?
hint: Only iron and a few other metals are magnetic. Plastic, wood and glass are not.

subject: science
question: Which of these is not attracted by a magnet?
hint: Copper is a metal but it is non-magnetic. Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic.

subject: science
question: Are all metals magnetic?
options: No, only some metals such as iron are magnetic
hint: This is a common mistake. Gold, silver, copper and aluminium are metals but are not magnetic.

subject: science
question: A magnet can be used to separate iron pins from a heap of sand because:
options: Iron is magnetic and sand is not
hint: Magnetic separation works whenever one part of a mixture is magnetic and the rest is not.

subject: science
question: Where is the pulling force of a bar magnet strongest?
hint: Iron filings cluster most thickly at the two ends, which are the poles.

subject: science
question: A freely suspended bar magnet always comes to rest pointing:
options: In a different direction each time
hint: The Earth behaves like a huge magnet, so a free magnet lines up north to south. This is how a compass works.

subject: science
question: When two like poles of magnets are brought close, they:
hint: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

subject: science
question: The north pole of one magnet is brought near the south pole of another. They will:
hint: Unlike poles attract, so north and south pull together.

subject: science
question: Which instrument uses a magnet to show direction?
hint: The magnetic needle of a compass settles along the north-south line.

subject: science
question: Which of these would a magnet pick up from a mixture?
hint: Steel contains iron, so it is attracted to a magnet.

subject: science
question: Which property makes copper suitable for electrical wiring?
options: It is a good conductor and is ductile
hint: Copper both carries current well and can be drawn into long thin wires.

subject: science
question: Why should you never touch an electric switch with wet hands?
options: Water conducts electricity and can give a shock
hint: Ordinary water contains dissolved salts, which let electricity pass through it and through you.

subject: science
question: Which of these best conducts electricity?
hint: Dissolved salts allow current to pass. Very pure water is actually a poor conductor.

subject: science
question: A woollen sweater keeps you warm in winter because wool:
options: Conducts heat quickly to your body
Traps air and is a poor conductor of heat
hint: Wool does not make heat. It traps air and slows the escape of your own body heat.

subject: science
question: A steel spoon left in hot tea becomes hot at the other end because steel:
hint: Heat travels through metals by conduction, from the hot end to the cooler end.

subject: science
question: Which pair of properties makes aluminium suitable for cooking foil?
options: Malleable and a good conductor of heat
hint: Foil must be beaten very thin and must let heat through to the food.

subject: science
question: Magnets lose their magnetism if they are:
options: Kept in a cool dry place
hint: Rough handling, heating and dropping all disturb the arrangement inside and weaken a magnet.

subject: science
question: Which of these uses a magnet in everyday life?
options: The door catch of a refrigerator
hint: A magnetic strip in the door seal holds a refrigerator door shut.

subject: science
question: If a magnet is broken into two pieces, each piece will:
options: Have both a north and a south pole
hint: You cannot separate the poles. Every piece of a magnet, however small, has two poles.

subject: science
question: Which test would tell you whether a shiny grey object is made of iron or aluminium?
hint: Both look similar, but only iron is attracted to a magnet.

subject: science
question: Scrap yards use large electromagnets to lift:
hint: Electromagnets attract only magnetic materials, which makes them ideal for sorting iron out of mixed scrap.
